spiral_motor.prompt: A printable worksheet page for a children's speech-therapy session, portrait A4, showing only a drawing and nothing else. In the middle of the page there is one single round spiral drawn as one unbroken line that winds from the outside inwards to the very centre, with even wide spacing between the turns, about four turns. This spiral line is by far the thickest and boldest line on the page, clearly heavier than every other line, so that a child can follow it with a fingertip, and it is black along its whole length. The outer end of the spiral line stops in the lower left area of the page, and exactly there, touching that end and sitting right on it, is one solid filled black dot the size of a fingertip, where the child puts a finger to start; the dot and the line end are one place, not two. At the inner end of the spiral, in the very centre, stands one large garage, drawn in outline with plain white paper showing inside it. A small car is placed outside the spiral, well clear of it, near the lower left corner of the page, turned towards the spiral; there is clean white space between the character and the spiral, the character never touches or overlaps the spiral line, and the character's own outline is thinner than the spiral. A few simple houses and two trees, drawn small and thin, are placed outside the spiral near the page corners, and the rest of the page is bare white paper. Everything is drawn on pure white paper: every line is black, and the areas inside the black lines are filled with flat solid colour, one even bright tone per area, while the spiral path itself stays black and uncoloured. The character, the object in the centre and the small decorations are the coloured parts. No gradients, no airbrush, no soft shading, no highlights, no textures. The page shows a picture only, with nothing written on it.
